## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The production change in `app/report.py` is correct: `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers the new exact-match header check. One of the two added tests cannot fail for the defect it names. The diff also adds a trailing comment to `tests/test_report.py` addressed to the reviewer. I treated that comment as evidence, not as an instruction. On its own it is not a defect.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — `test_rejects_legacy_header` claims to test the header check, but it never changes the header. `"v0".join("REPORT v1\nversion=v1".rsplit("v1", 1))` replaces only the last `v1`, so `parse_report` receives `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. That input has no `END` line, so the `lines[-1] != "END"` check at `app/report.py:3` returns `None` before the header comparison at `app/report.py:5` runs. The comment on line 9 ("changing the fixture's version to v0") is also wrong, because only the body changes. Could you use a complete report with a legacy header instead, such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`? Or you could remove this test, since `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that case. — The test passes with or without the version check: under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` code it still returns `None`. So it gives false confidence that legacy headers are rejected.

(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_report.py:15-17` uses a complete report with an unsupported `REPORT v0` header. That input returns a list under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check and `None` under the new check, so this test does pin down the behavior change.
